title: Python: two nonlocal writers plus an unrecorded del leave a local's binding count wrong; 6d and R4 resolve to the wrong class (reproduced on dev e13f2f8)
description:
Found in the GCLI-113 round 2 review (F4) and reproduced here on origin/dev e13f2f8 (R4 landed at c84ad89). applyScopeRedirects (calls.ts ~1690-1729) moves each nonlocal write onto the nearest enclosing function that already records a binding of the name, deepest scope first; the walker records no `del`, and `del x` makes x local to its function in Python. So with two nonlocal writers the deeper one finds no recorded binding up the chain and falls back to the nearest function, while the other lands on the function that holds the name: that function then counts fewer bindings than the text has, and a single or all-C() count resolves to the wrong class. REPRODUCTION (class C and D each define run; app.py), source A: `def g():
    def h():
        def k():
            nonlocal x
            x = D()
        k()
    def h2():
        nonlocal x
        x = C()
    h()
    x.run()
    del x` : the site x.run() resolves to C.run (rule 6d on the single binding that arrived with origin h2); at run time h() runs k, so x is a D and the call is D.run. Source B adds `def h3(): nonlocal x; x = C()` : R4 resolves x.run() to C.run (two C() bindings, k's D() write misplaced onto h). Both fixtures resolve the wrong class today. Also from the review: with the unrecorded del, `def e(): f = m.func` plus nested `def g(): f(); del f` emits an edge for a call that raises UnboundLocalError (shared with every name rule). ALIAS (GCLI-113) refuses any binding that carries origin, so it is unaffected. The root fix (record del targets as bindings in the walker) moves counts for every rule and is a design choice for opum-doc, not started here; the interim options are for the leader and opum-doc. Rules that read origin: R4 localConstructedClass (origin for the constructor name); rule 6d knownClassOf reads the single binding's scope without origin.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the two reproductions (sources A and B in the description) leave x.run() unresolved by 6d and R4 respectively, each with a refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site and the bin is unchanged, and a positive twin where every writer is C()
a decision recorded from opum-doc on the route (record del in the walker, or refuse a binding that carries origin in 6d and R4 as ALIAS does) before any build
a per-site five-pin corpus diff naming any site that moves
